q.metric: Q = mean over the 8 builds of (scenarios passed / scenarios of runtime-abc-rep that the build was scored on); a build that did not start counts 0 and is reported apart; flakes are left out as in flakeRule
q.ceilingNote: ceiling = Q >= 95 (calibrate-80's ceilingPct). Basis: lap 13 (A alone, 495 words) 100.0 %; calibrate-80's opus minimum 90.6 % over 12 requests of 694-901 words and 96.2 % at L2; here 1,658 words (L1), three parts, ~45 scenarios, part C new (nothing to copy from training), parts B and C leave details to the builder. The side is the less likely to be wrong by the evidence (P(Q < 90) = 0.35 < 0.5); it was not chosen to split.
q.bandNote: pBelow90 = 0.35 includes about 0.10 for a lap-invalidating fault (dependency-resolution, fake-service-infrastructure) that would show as a Q far below 90 for every build; the builder-caused share is about 0.25-0.30. One failing scenario of 45 costs a build 2.2 points, so Q below 90 needs about 4-5 failed scenarios per build on average (or 1 in 2-3 builds failing a whole part).

whereItFalls.note: Where the first failing scenario of a build is expected, as probabilities that at least one build (of 8) fails at least one scenario for that reason. They do not sum to 1. dependency-resolution, fake-service-infrastructure and base-move are lap-invalidating (infrastructure, not a builder verdict); expectation-error sites go to errors.json.

successLine.text: The lap 'held' (factory carried over to an existing Python repository at a size that may split) when all of: (1) Q >= 90 % (owner); (2) at least 7 of the 8 builds started (builderOk); (3) no lap-invalidating fault (dependency-resolution, fake-service-infrastructure or base-move) in any scored scenario; (4) the run shipped (owner: the ship stays a condition): runtime-abc-run ended with a fast-forward of the ship target whose new HEAD is the judged commit and which has 003efef as an ancestor. Otherwise 'did not hold', and the report names the site of the first failure by the whereItFalls list. A lap-invalidating fault is not a verdict on the builder: it is reported as invalid and the replicate is run again under a new change id after the fault is fixed.

errorsRule: Errors rule (lap 8, restated): an expected value that contradicts the request, or a count or number that does not add up, is an expectation error; so is a run step whose expectation depends on a file or a template path the shown ranges do not give, an expectation that depends on a reading the request leaves open (decide-argv-values: the form of --state-dir; ntfy-config-validation: `enabled` false with a bad topic) or on the clock (clock-and-ladder), and an expectation of what the event's title or body say that the shown code does not give. Each is listed in errors.json with a quote of the request; the whole scenario is left out of every build's pass fraction. Q is reported both raw and corrected; if they fall on different sides of 90 %, the verdict is 'undecided', not either.
flakeRule: Flake rule (lap 12, restated): each build is rescored twice after its first judgement (replicate --rescore twice, judgements = 3). A (scenario, build) whose pass/fail differs among the 3 is a flake and is left out of that build's pass fraction (numerator and denominator). More than 5 % of the cells being flakes gives no verdict.

contamination.kind: reproduction of two published changes (A, B: back-in-time) and one forward-looking change (C)
contamination.text: Both subjects are public in suisya-systems/claude-org-runtime: A is #242 / issue #240 (merged 2026-10-11), B is #245 / issue #244 (merged 2026-10-12); both released in v0.1.50. A model may have seen them, so Q can be an upper bound on what the builder derives from the request alone. Leak paths: (1) model training data, not testable here; (2) the builder's model session shares the host network (factory README), so a builder could read the published fix or `pip download` a released wheel of claude-org-runtime; the run contract tells it to install nothing and use no network, an instruction only; (3) the ship target holds no object after 003efef. B's section of docs/cli.md is not in the base (it was added by the change), so the base holds no written answer to B. The request states the rules of both changes in its own words, so the builder is not asked to rediscover them. Part C (runtime #21, ntfy) is forward-looking: no commit of the repository implements it (`git grep -i ntfy`: 0 lines at 003efef and at 719f865), so a leak by fetch has nothing to find except the issue text; the ntfy HTTP API itself is public knowledge, so C is not free of training-data influence. Q is reported by part so that the forward-looking part can be read apart.
contamination.check: after the replicate and the run, every builder transcript under $FACTORY_HOME/transcripts/<change>/ (factory prerequisite 1) is searched; the commands are in runbook step 10. Search terms: `github.com/suisya-systems/claude-org-runtime`, `raw.githubusercontent`, `pypi.org`, `pip download`, `pip install`, `git fetch`, `git log --all`, the commit ids b6ad40a / 263ff3f / 410fd8a / 176bcf1 / a021ebd / 719f865 / f79286f, the tags v0.1.50 / v0.1.51, the issue numbers #240 / #242 / #244 / #245, and the tool names WebFetch / WebSearch. Any hit lists the build apart and Q is given with and without it. A transcript that is missing for a build is itself reported (the check is then incomplete, not clean). The check is on the transcript, the output-side search over the build's diff (as in lap 13) is run too.
